questions.q: Citizenship provisions are given in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
Citizenship (Articles 5–11) is dealt with in Part II of the Constitution.
Context: Part I covers the Union and its territory, Part III Fundamental Rights, Part IV Directive Principles.

**Answer: Part II**

questions.q: Who has the power to create new states and alter boundaries of existing states?
questions.solution:
Under Article 3, Parliament may form new states and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states by a simple majority, on the President's prior recommendation. The concerned state's view is sought but is not binding.

**Answer: Parliament**
questions.shortcut: Article 3 → Parliament's power over state boundaries.

questions.q: Which deity is predominantly worshipped through Manipuri dance?
questions.solution:
Manipuri dance grew out of the Vaishnavite tradition of Manipur; its central theme is the Ras Leela, the divine dance of Radha and Krishna, so Krishna is the deity predominantly worshipped through it.

**Answer: Krishna**

questions.q: Which of the following is a key characteristic of Bhangra music?
questions.solution:
Bhangra, the folk dance-music of Punjab (performed at harvest, driven by the dhol), is characterised by fast, vigorous, energetic beats — not slow or purely melodic tunes.

**Answer: Fast and energetic beats**

questions.q: In which year did the Jaipur Literature Festival begin?
questions.solution:
The Jaipur Literature Festival was first held in 2006, growing out of the Jaipur Virasat Foundation; it is co-directed by Namita Gokhale and William Dalrymple and bills itself as the world's largest free literary festival.

**Answer: 2006**

questions.q: Which river of India has the largest catchment area?
questions.solution:
The Ganga has the largest catchment area among Indian rivers (roughly 8.6 lakh sq km, draining the whole northern plain). The Godavari, at about 3.1 lakh sq km, is the largest among the peninsular rivers.

**Answer: Ganga**

questions.q: Which of the following plate boundaries formed the Himalayas?
questions.solution:
The Himalayas rose at a convergent (colliding) plate boundary: the northward-drifting Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate, folding up the sediments of the Tethys Sea.

**Answer: Convergent boundary**
questions.shortcut: Mountains at colliding plates: Himalayas = Indian–Eurasian convergence.

questions.q: Why are the days on Venus longer than its years?
options: Venus has a slower rotation than revolution
Venus revolves very slowly around the Sun
Venus spins on its axis in the opposite direction
questions.solution:
Venus spins extremely slowly — one rotation takes about 243 Earth days — while it orbits the Sun in about 225 days. Because its rotation is slower than its revolution, a (solar) day on Venus outlasts its year.

**Answer: Venus has a slower rotation than revolution**

questions.q: Which mosque within Agra Fort was constructed by Shah Jahan for the royal ladies and features three domes?
questions.solution:
Nagina Masjid (the 'Gem Mosque') in Agra Fort is a small white-marble mosque with three domes, built by Shah Jahan as a private place of prayer for the ladies of the royal household (the Mina Bazaar for the zenana lay just below it).

**Answer: Nagina Masjid**

questions.q: Which planet has a magnetic field that is offset from its center and tilted about 59 degrees to its rotational axis?
questions.solution:
Voyager 2 discovered that Uranus's magnetic field is offset from the planet's centre and inclined about 59 degrees to its rotational axis (the axis itself is tipped about 98 degrees, so Uranus effectively rolls along its orbit).

**Answer: Uranus**

questions.q: What is the maximum duration of a standard boxing bout in the Olympics?
questions.solution:
An Olympic boxing bout consists of three rounds of 3 minutes each — a maximum of 9 minutes of boxing — for both men's and women's events.

**Answer: Three 3-minute rounds**

questions.q: How many Asian Games medals did India win in shooting at Hangzhou 2023?
questions.solution:
Indian shooters won 22 medals at the Hangzhou 2023 Asian Games — 7 gold, 9 silver and 6 bronze — their best-ever Asian Games haul and the largest share of India's 107-medal tally.

**Answer: 22**

questions.q: Blood is classified under which type of animal tissue?
questions.solution:
Blood is a fluid connective tissue: its cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) are suspended in a fluid matrix (plasma), which connects body parts and transports gases, nutrients and wastes.

**Answer: Connective tissue**
questions.shortcut: Blood = connective tissue with liquid matrix (plasma).

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of chemotropism in plants?
questions.solution:
Chemotropism is growth towards or away from a chemical stimulus. The classic example is the pollen tube growing towards the ovule (guided by chemical signals/sugars) during fertilisation. Shoots bending to light is phototropism, roots growing down is geotropism, and leaf folding on touch is thigmonasty.

**Answer: Pollen tube growing towards ovule**

questions.q: The Chipko Movement is associated with:
questions.solution:
The Chipko Movement (born in Uttarakhand in 1973, with village women hugging trees and leaders like Sunderlal Bahuguna) was a forest conservation movement against commercial tree felling.

**Answer: Forest conservation**

questions.q: The Rs. 6000 crores allocated for One Nation One Subscription initiative ensures smooth implementation of ONOS from 1st January 2025 to 31st December _______.
questions.solution:
The Union Cabinet approved the One Nation One Subscription scheme in November 2024 with about Rs 6,000 crore for three years, giving institutions access to subscribed international journals from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027.

**Answer: 2027**

questions.q: Which crop did the British force the peasants of Maharashtra to produce?
questions.solution:
In Maharashtra (the Deccan), British policies pushed peasants into growing cotton for the mills of Manchester — cultivation boomed during the American Civil War (1861–65) — and the resulting debt trap later sparked the Deccan Riots of 1875.

**Answer: Cotton**
questions.shortcut: Deccan → cotton; Bengal → jute; Assam → tea.

questions.q: In which year the World Parliament of Religions was held in Chicago?
questions.solution:
Swami Vivekananda addressed the World Parliament of Religions at Chicago in September 1893, beginning with his famous 'Sisters and brothers of America' speech.

**Answer: 1893**

questions.q: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic silver medal?
questions.solution:
P. V. Sindhu became the first Indian woman to win an Olympic silver medal, finishing second in badminton at Rio 2016 (she later added a bronze at Tokyo 2020).

**Answer: P. V. Sindhu**
questions.shortcut: Sindhu = silver (Rio 2016); Karnam Malleswari = first woman medallist (bronze, 2000).

questions.q: Which of the following ministry has unveiled 'Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS) 2024' Report?
options: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
questions.solution:
The LEADS ('Logistics Ease Across Different States') report is an annual perception-based logistics index brought out by the Logistics Division, DPIIT, under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

**Answer: Ministry of Commerce & Industry**
